record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
record.original_question: How should neutrino experiments report CCQE measurements with precise definitions of the event selection, observables, and the meaning of “CCQE,” while providing model-independent quantities and flux information that theorists can calculate directly, so that comparisons with neutrino and electron-scattering theory are unambiguous?

evidence.quote:
It is essential to reduce any barrier between the reported measurements
and the quantities that can be predicted from theory. There has already
been signiﬁcant progress in moving from measurements of eﬀective param-
eters to more model-independent quantities that can be directly calculated
by theorists with neutrino ﬂux predictions provided by experimentalists.
It will be critical for all experimental eﬀorts to engage and continuously
develop this interface in order to provide theorists with the most eﬀective
input.

We have seen that precisely deﬁning what is meant by “CCQE” in a
measurement is critical for interpreting the results. Clarity in the event
selection and observables will become even more important as engagement
continues with theorists and the electron scattering community, where
terms such as “quasi-elastic scattering” and “ﬁnal state interactions” may
mean something substantially diﬀerent.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In neutrino-nucleus scattering experiments, charged-current quasi-elastic (CCQE) interactions are conventionally identified by an event selection that targets a charged lepton plus one (or zero) outgoing nucleons with no detected mesons in the final state. Because nuclear effects, final-state interactions, and detector thresholds blur the distinction between the underlying elementary process and what is actually observed, the operational meaning of "CCQE" varies between experiments and differs from the usage in the electron-scattering community.

Devise a reporting framework for CCQE measurements that makes experiment–theory comparison unambiguous. Specifically, formulate:

1. A precise definition of the event-selection topology in terms of observable final-state particles (lepton kinematics, nucleon multiplicity and momentum thresholds, photon and meson vetoes), independent of any underlying interaction model.

2. A set of model-independent observables (e.g., differential cross sections in directly measured kinematic variables of the outgoing lepton and hadrons) that a theorist can compute from first principles without needing to replicate the experiment's neutrino-generator assumptions.

3. A specification of the incoming neutrino flux Φ(E_ν), including its uncertainties and correlations, in a form that can be convolved with any theoretical cross-section model dσ/dΩ(E_ν, …) to yield a prediction directly comparable to the reported observables.

4. A clear statement distinguishing the experimental "CCQE-like" topology from the theoretical notion of quasi-elastic scattering (one-body current on a single nucleon) and from the electron-scattering usage of "quasi-elastic" and "final-state interactions."

The problem is to produce such a reporting protocol—definitions, observables, flux deliverables, and unfolding/acceptance conventions—so that comparisons of CCQE measurements with both neutrino- and electron-scattering theoretical predictions become unambiguous and reproducible.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a community-level methodology recommendation rather than a single solvable theorem. Subsequent work by the NuSTEC collaboration and various neutrino-experiment whitepapers has advanced model-independent reporting (e.g., flux-folded differential cross sections, transverse-kinematic-imbalance variables, and standardized flux releases), but a fully unified, universally adopted CCQE reporting framework remains an ongoing effort.

status_evidence.title: NuSTEC White Paper: Status and Challenges of Neutrino–Nucleus Scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the need for model-independent reporting and improved experiment-theory interface in neutrino-nucleus scattering, including CCQE.
status_evidence.claim: The community continues to work on standardizing model-independent CCQE reporting; not fully resolved.
